groups.label: Legumes
groups.note: They fix nitrogen: put them before leafy greens, which need a lot of nitrogen.

groups.label: Leafy greens
groups.note: They need fair nitrogen: they do well after a legume.

groups.label: Nightshades (fruits and potato)
groups.note: They share pests and diseases (and with potato): let several seasons pass before repeating.

groups.label: Cucurbits (fruits)
groups.note: They take up space and exhaust the bed: follow them with a legume or leafy greens.

groups.label: Roots
groups.note: They loosen the soil deeper down: they do well after leafy greens.

groups.label: Alliums (bulbs)
groups.note: Not very demanding: they close the rotation well before starting over.

rules: Do not plant the same family in the same bed two seasons in a row: it builds up soil pests and diseases.
After a legume (pea, bean) plant leafy greens: they use the nitrogen it left behind.
Alternate families that feed differently and have different roots (fruits, leaves, roots, legumes).
With nightshades (tomato, potato, pepper) let several seasons pass before repeating them in the same spot.
source: INTA Pro-Huerta: rotación de cultivos en la huerta familiar (orientativo, a validar localmente)
